questions.stem:
In modern times, the use of pankhas has been restricted to decorative purposes, and they have become traditional craft items in India. questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your Art Club is going to hold a pankha exhibition-cum-workshop in the school, in which fans from different states will be on show and students may try their hand at making one. Write a notice for your school notice board announcing it. (100 words)

markingPoints.description: Content: the notice announces a pankha exhibition-cum-workshop, names the states whose fans will be on show and says that students may try making a fan
Format: a capitalised heading such as NOTICE, the title of the event, the body of the notice in clear short paragraphs and the issuing body's signature at the end
Organisation: the details are arranged in a sensible order, that is, what the event is, what will be on show, what visitors can do and why it is useful
Accuracy: correct spelling, punctuation, capital letters and a formal and concise tone suitable for a notice board
Expression: simple sentences and suitable vocabulary that invite every student to attend and to take part in the workshop

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
NOTICE
PANKHA EXHIBITION-CUM-WORKSHOP

All students are invited to a Pankha Exhibition-cum-Workshop being held by the Art Club of our school. Come and see the hand fans of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha and Bihar, and find out how each one is made. Fans of bamboo, cane, palm leaf, silk, brass, leather and silver, with decorative beads and stones, will be on show. Artisans will also guide you as you try your hand at making a fan yourself. Pankha-making workshops like this one help spread awareness about the beauty and importance of this craft. Everyone is welcome.

Sd/- Art Club

evidence: Initiatives such as pankha-making workshops, both within and outside the handicraft exhibitions help spread awareness about the beauty and importance of this craft in India’s culture.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
To: The Principal
Subject: Permission to hold a pankha exhibition-cum-workshop

Respected Sir,
We, the students of this school, request you to allow us to hold a pankha exhibition-cum-workshop in the school premises. Fans from different states will be on show, such as the appliqué hand fan of Rajasthan, the mirror work and beads fans of Gujarat, the leather fans of Kutch, sola hand fans of West Bengal and the Phadh hand fans of Uttar Pradesh. We would also like artisans to demonstrate how each fan is made. Such workshops, held within and outside handicraft exhibitions, spread awareness about the beauty and importance of this craft, and the demand they create gives our artisans a livelihood. We therefore request you kindly to grant us permission.

Yours obediently,
A student

PANKHA: WHERE THE WIND CARRIES A STORY

Come and see the hand fans of India! On show are the appliqué hand fan of Rajasthan, its zardozi hand fan worked in gold threadwork, and temple hand fans made by engraving brass, with a long handle. The word punkha or pankha originates from the word ‘pankh’, which means feather of a bird. Pankha is used to refer to all fans, whereas the word pankhi denotes a small plumed fan used in ancient India. Evidence of the existence and use of pankhi in India can be found in Buddhist wall paintings at Ajanta. These wall paintings date back to the 2nd century CE.
